tcn.architecture_features_inference: by Huseyin Umut Isik (team member): github.com/ata-yunus-ortak/football-video-analysis, branch mtah-possession, commit 167dc7b198c094c2eb1db5cd7ed8a852f603f867 (possession/train.py, features.py, infer.py, decode.py): 37 team-symmetric features per frame, dilated temporal convolution network at 12.5 Hz (stem conv 5, 14 residual blocks of dilated conv 3 + GroupNorm 8 + GELU + dropout 0.15 + conv 1, hidden 128, 1x1 head; three outputs team 0 / team 1 / dead), NumPy float64 inference with probabilities averaged over members and both team orders and rounded to 4 decimals. Byte copies of his inference modules are used unchanged.
tcn.weights: trained by us on 14 Nov 2026 with v214/tcn_jax.py, a JAX re-implementation of his training (PyTorch could not be installed in this environment): AdamW (weight decay 1e-2), one-cycle learning rate up to 2e-3 (30% warm-up, cosine), gradient clipping 1.0, crops of 2048 steps, batch 16, cross-entropy. Differences from his script: constant Adam momentum 0.9 (PyTorch's OneCycleLR also cycles it between 0.85 and 0.95); JAX / NumPy initialisation and random streams; twelve replicas per half (six of his simulator, six of ours; odd replicas with the teams exchanged) and six epochs instead of six replicas and twelve epochs (the same number of optimisation steps per training match); our prepared data has no ball height, so the height term of his simulator is inactive. The JAX network was compared with his NumPy inference on random input and random weights (largest absolute difference of the probabilities 7.9e-7; float32 against float64).
tcn.training_data: open DFL data only (Bassek et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0), as prepared for the v2 models; labels = the provider's flags. Replicas: his simulator (tcn/degrade.py, every half on its own, seed 1000 * match + 10 * half + replica) and ours (possession/degrade.py, v2 profile, seed 500000 + 1000 * match + replica). dfl4_both_s{0,1,2}: J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WPY, J03WQQ (the four matches of the v2 validation models). dfl6_both_s{0,1,2}: those four plus J03WN1 and J03WR9 (the six matches of the released v2 bundles). No Metrica game, no PFF game, not J03WMX, nothing of the provided match.
tcn.weights_if_selected: dfl6_both_s0, s1, s2 merged into one file (three members), with the released v2 bundles; nothing is trained after the decision

fusion_rule_fixed_before_any_score.source: v215/pooling.py (the file that would be released as possession/pooling.py; v214/fuse2.py with another weight and docstring)
steps: v2 side: second-stage P(dead) and P(home | alive), rounded to 6 decimals, exactly what the v2.11 decoder is given
three classes: home = (1 - P(dead)) * P(home | alive), away = (1 - P(dead)) * (1 - P(home | alive)), dead = P(dead)
TCN probabilities (12.5 Hz, 4 decimals) linearly interpolated to the 25 fps frame grid (tcn/decode.upsample), per play block
pooled P(dead) = dead / sum, pooled P(home | alive) = home / (home + away), both rounded to 6 decimals
possession.decode: emissions + Viterbi per play block with the constants of the path (v2.1: switch 3, entry / exit 60, dead bias -0.3); D outside the blocks
v2.3 path (measured noise above 0.30 m): not pooled; the labels are the v2.11 labels
fusion_rule_fixed_before_any_score.tcn_input: the tracking the v2 models see: packed slots, after the goalkeeper team check, with the filled ball when the 0.50 m gate opened; never smoothed; metres from the pitch centre, float32, NaN where missing; team 0 = home slots

Result: weights without a copy below -0.007: ari10, ari20; largest mean among them: ari20 (+0.0138); its mean on the 20 DFL copies: +0.0135, on the 16 tactical DFL copies: +0.0125.

decision_rule: All seven gates pass: the pooled system with this weight is selected and integrated as possession-v2.15 (new entry point and manifest; byte copies of the inference modules of commit 167dc7b; the three dfl6_both members with the registered SHA-256; v2.11k becomes the next step of the technical ladder). It replaces v2.11k in the delivery only if, by 16 Nov 2026 23:59 Istanbul, the ported inference runs under Python 3.10 / numpy 1.26.4, the output on synthetic provided-like bundles is byte-identical across Python 3.10 / numpy 1.26.4 and Python 3.13 / numpy 2.5.3, the full test suite passes, a full-size chain rehearsal ends OK, and the documents describe the second model, its training data and the three attempts; and only if the delivery chain then runs OK on the team's computer. Otherwise v2.11k stays. Any gate fails: v2.11k stays the release, the candidate is recorded as tried and not used, and no further candidate with the second model is registered before the deadline. The gates are applied once, to all rows; nothing is re-run with other seeds, weights, pools or decoder constants.
reported_alongside: every row; means per source (DFL, Metrica) in every condition; the TCN alone; recall of possessions under 2 s and under 1 s; transition F1 at 12 / 25 frames; numbers of predicted spells; frames changed; noise path and goalkeeper moves per copy
Metrica game 3 and PFF game 3839 after the decision (not gates)
not_part_of_this_validation: The Smart Tagging kick-off rule: it cannot be measured on external data; it stays as in v2.11k.
The pooling on the v2.3 path: not measured, therefore not used there.
The provided match: not read, not run and not scored by this validation.
limits: Third attempt with the same gates. Each validation used new copies, but a gate that looks at single copies (G4) is passed more easily by a design that is tried again with a more cautious setting; a pass here is weaker evidence than a pass at the first attempt would have been. The weight was chosen on development copies with a margin, not by trying weights on the copies of this validation, and no further attempt follows.

The validation matches were used for every earlier selection of v2.x, for the development of the TCN recipe by its author, for the development of v2.14 and, through the copies of the v2.14 validation, for the choice of this weight. Only the copies are new. This is a validation, not a fresh test.

There is no untouched test for the pooled system: J03WMX was used in the TCN recipe's development by its author, and Metrica game 3 in the development of v2.14 and of this candidate. The registered final test of v2.11k on J03WMX would not describe a released v2.15; its plan would have to be re-registered, and such a run could only be reported as not fresh for the TCN family.

The plans of v2.12 and v2.13 named 14 Nov 2026 23:59 Istanbul as the last moment for a change of release. This plan sets a later one (16 Nov 23:59) at the team lead's request; the cost is less time for the checks on the team's computer.

The weights were trained by the process that validates them; nobody else has checked the training script. PyTorch and JAX runs of the same recipe are not bit-identical, and a JAX run is not bit-reproducible across machines; the released weights are the files with the registered SHA-256, not a re-run.
Corruption, slot packing, camera window and broadcast camera are simulated by us; the provided tracking may differ. The second model was shown the two simulators of the team and nothing else.
DFL labels are the provider's per-frame flags; Metrica labels are our event-derived proxies.

The reserve configuration without the kick-off rule (possession-release-graded-windows.json) stays the v2.11g ladder. If the rule written down in K011 sends the team to that reserve (a failed Smart Tagging check on the team's computer), the second model is not used either.

NumPy matrix products are not guaranteed bit-identical across BLAS builds; the 4-decimal and 6-decimal rounding makes a different output unlikely, not impossible. Checked only by the integration tests named in the decision rule.
